title: Directives on cutting indigenous trees
rule: The Minister may direct the occupier of land held under a right of occupancy to stop cutting indigenous trees, to cut in a set way, or to replant.
points: Reasons: fire, climate or soil erosion; water supply; natural regeneration; loss of biodiversity; general environmental damage; timber shortage.
A directive can cover the method and route of cutting, a ban or restriction, and afforestation.
If the occupier fails to replant in time, the Minister may have it done and the cost is a debt owed by the occupier.
The occupier may appeal to the High Court.
